text:
ashley: quick heads-up 1: pharma customer wants immutable audit trails for 7 years, BYOK with HSM attestation, and a legal-hold API that can lock records across regions. theyre asking for retrieval proofs for any re-identification.
tanvi: that's a strict ask. propose we offer two delivery patterns: live-retain (hot) for 90d + searchable metadata for 7y, or cold-archive with WORM + signed manifest and 24-72h restore SLA. customers pick per-tenant. :balance_scale:
lee: security note: re-identification keys must never live on our control plane for hosted customers. envelope encryption where customer KMS unwraps a per-tenant key at restore time is the only acceptable path for auditors.
mike: ops constraints: cross-region legal holds mean we need a global index of hold-state and an idempotent snapshot job. this impacts throughput on export pipeline. small sketch: global-hold-table -> snapshot-fanout -> archive-writer.
ash: question: can we meet SOC2 evidence requirements with signed manifests + HSM attestation?
tanvi: yes if we capture: key attestation chain, manifest SHA256, timestamped signatures, and audit logs for who requested re-id and why. auditors will want proof that the key access required to re-id was authorized.
ash: ok. UX/PRD idea: add a tenant-level "evidence policy" with options:
  - retention_profile: hot-90d/cold-7y
  - byok_mode: enforced/optional
  - legal_hold_ttl: indefinite/expiry
  - reid_requires_approval: true/false
lee: sample API payload for policy and legal hold:

``
POST /v1/admin/tenants/123/policy
{
  "retention_profile": "cold-7y",
  "byok_mode": "enforced",
  "legal_hold": {
    "enabled": true,
    "comment": "FDA audit",
    "applied_by": "ops@pharmaX.com"
  }
}

POST /v1/admin/tenants/123/legal_hold/snapshot
{
  "snapshot_label": "fda-2026-03",
  "regions": ["us-east-1","eu-west-1"]
}
```

mike: acceptance criteria proposal:
  - per-tenant policy stored and enforced by routing layer
  - archived manifests include SHA256, signed by HSM-backed key, and a KMS attestation chain string
  - legal-hold snapshot API returns a signed manifest and store location; export tests reproduce a 3rd-party verification step
  - retrieval runbook with roles, approval flow, and audit entry creation
  - cost estimator that shows hot vs cold delta per TB/yr
ash: scheduling: recommend a 3-sprint pilot (spike + prototype + compliance verification). deliverables by sprint end:
  - spike: envelope-byok feasibility + cross-region snapshot design (lee, sprint 1)
  - proto: implement snapshot + manifest signing + cold write (mike, sprint 2)
  - compliance: run export tests, create SOC2 evidence pack, and ops runbook (tanvi, sprint 3)
ops-bot: Note: archival pipeline will be in maintenance window next Fri 01:00-03:00 UTC. plan snapshots accordingly. :calendar:
ash: risks to call out in PRD:
  - cost of keeping metadata searchable for 7 years (indexing vs blob store tradeoff)
  - latency for restores from cold tier impacting SLAs
  - complexity of customer KMS onboarding (permissions, cross-cloud keys)

tanvi: mitigations:
  - default to metadata-only searchable index with retention-tiered TTLs; offer paid-hot-retention add-on
  - define restore-class tiers (standard 48h, expedited 4h) with pricing table
  - provide a KMS onboarding checklist and automated verifier to reduce human errors

ash: action items:
  - ashley: draft brief PRD and proposal slides (due Tue COB)
  - lee: run envelope-KMS spike + handoff notes (2w)
  - mike: prototype snapshot signer and cold-writer (3w)
  - tanvi: compliance test harness and SOC2 evidence template (3w)
  - ops-bot: schedule archival maintenance exceptions for pilot runs

ashley: adding long-term cost estimate request to ops task. we'll sync next Wed to review spike results. :rocket:
